content.title: Greenland Escalation Risks a Different Kind of Trade War. How It Could Play Out.
content.summary: The tariff tit-for-tat is back, this time between the U.S. and Europe as President Donald Trump amps up the pressure on the continent in his effort to annex Greenland, a territory controlled by NATO ally Denmark.  One big reason tariffs didn’t create as much pain last year as economists anticipated was that the levies the president rolled out didn’t turn into a trade war.  Few countries retaliated and when China, the outlier, did, it ultimately led to a ratcheting down of tensions.
